key_highlights: ASX closed the week lower as traders priced in further RBA rate hikes, with commentary urging caution before another increase given a stalling economy
Australian banks forecast the largest house price falls on record; CBA reports home loan applications down 15% since the federal budget
Iron ore sector faces a structural shakeout masked by geopolitical conflict; Macarthur clears WA bulk test hurdle
Bathla's collapse signals broader construction-sector stress, described as symptomatic of a 'Ponzi economy' in housing
ASIC launches review of whistleblower complaints at Big 4 accounting firms, raising governance concerns
Energy transition costs mounting; TMK Energy gas rates surge on Mongolian drilling; Beetaloo gas cartel scrutiny intensifies
Small-cap activity strong: Kaoko Metals, Vanadium Resources, Piche, Aurum, Brightstar, Solstice, Power Minerals in focus
Trump's Fed ultimatum and Strait of Hormuz oil crisis add global volatility; Bitcoin $80K breakout failed post-jobs data

sectors.trend: Iron ore shakeout underway amid geopolitical distraction; small-cap explorers (Kaoko, Vanadium, Piche, Aurum, Brightstar, Solstice, Power Minerals) showing relative strength
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin pressure from structural demand shift; small-cap gold and critical-mines names offer tactical upside but carry execution risk

sectors.trend: CBA flags 15% drop in home loan applications; banks project record house price declines; ASIC Big 4 review adds governance overhang; CBA/Westpac fee practices under scrutiny
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, WBC.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX face credit-cycle headwinds and NIM compression; defensive dividend appeal intact but growth outlook weakens

sectors.trend: Energy transition costs 'running off the rails'; TMK Energy gas rates surge; Beetaloo gas cartel scrutiny; Strait of Hormuz crisis lifts oil
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WDS.AX, SXG.AX benefit from gas pricing; TMK.AX and Beetaloo (BTL.AX) in focus; transition-cost overhang pressures utilities

sectors.trend: Bathla collapse signals sector-wide stress; housing construction to follow prices lower; Victoria debt flagged by ratings agencies; Melbourne councils admit infrastructure shortfall
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) and builders (WBC.AX exposure, listed contractors) face demand contraction; rate-sensitive housing cycle turning

sectors.trend: EV sales overtake petrol cars in Australia for first time; hidden costs (charging, insurance) emerging; fuel-cost avoidance driving demand
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WDW.AX see fuel-volume headwinds; EV infrastructure and charging names gain relevance; consumer spending under pressure

sectors.trend: Nvidia confirms AI boom persists; Australia faces AI-worker and tradie shortages; big tech data-centre backlash grows
sectors.implications: Limited direct ASX exposure; CSL.AX, WES.AX benefit from AI-driven healthcare/logistics; skills shortage supports wage inflation

key_themes: RBA rate path uncertainty – market pricing higher-for-longer despite stalling growth
Housing cycle inflection – record price falls forecast, loan applications collapsing
Construction sector fragility – Bathla as canary in the coal mine
Iron ore structural shakeout vs geopolitical noise
Energy transition cost overhang and gas pricing dynamics
ASIC governance scrutiny of Big 4 accountants
Trump-Fed trade-war threat adding global risk premium

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA further rate hike despite weak growth
risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight short-duration bonds; reduce rate-sensitive REIT and construction exposure; monitor RBA statement language
Reduce bank equity weight; favour banks with lower housing exposure (ANZ.AX, NAB.AX); watch NIM and credit-loss provisions
Avoid listed construction names; monitor ASX 300 building sub-index for further defaults
Maintain commodity hedges; hold gold (GOLD.AX, NVG.AX) as hedge; diversify away from single-commodity exposure

risk_assessment.risk_factor: ASIC Big 4 review spilling into ASX governance
risk_assessment.mitigation: Review audit-firm exposure in holdings; favour companies with independent audit committees
Prefer cash-generative energy producers (WES.AX, WDS.AX) over transition-stage names

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold and critical-mines small caps
opportunities.rationale: Geopolitical risk premium, iron ore shakeout, and small-cap momentum (Kaoko, Vanadium, Piche, Aurum) support tactical upside

opportunities.recommendation: Add gas-exposed energy names on Hormuz premium
opportunities.rationale: TMK gas rate surge and Beetaloo cartel scrutiny lift gas pricing; WES and WDS benefit from structural gas demand

opportunities.recommendation: Selective bank accumulation on housing-cycle dip
opportunities.rationale: Record house-price fall forecasts create overhang but also set up mean-reversion; ANZ and NAB have lower housing beta

defensive_moves.rationale: Housing construction following prices lower; Bathla collapse signals sector fragility; Victoria debt concerns add sovereign overhang

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge rate risk with short-duration fixed income
defensive_moves.rationale: RBA may hike again despite weak growth; ASX already pricing higher-for-longer
Iron ore shakeout structural; war masking underlying demand weakness; diversify into multi-commodity or services

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain under pressure as RBA rate expectations and housing-cycle data dominate. Iron ore volatility and Hormuz oil spike add noise. Small-cap mining rotation provides pockets of strength. Expect choppy, range-bound trading with downside bias into RBA meeting.
market_outlook.long_term: Housing correction and construction stress could weigh on financials and REITs through 2026-27. Energy transition cost overhang and gas pricing support WES/WDS. Gold and critical-mines offer structural tailwinds. 'Bull case returns' narrative contingent on RBA pivoting and housing stabilising.
